codex.problem: The validator rejects two equal-specificity overlapping entries without checking whether either can actually be maximal. From schedule-cleanupFalse in tests/support/r13_schema_cases.json form three entries A/B/C, all with the original one-element path (inc8 interface hash, point entry:0), step=1, phase="fwd", generated=0 and kind="cleanup". A: iteration="*", realisation="reverse". B: iteration="*", realisation="recompute". C: iteration=[], realisation="reverse". The point is outside every loop, so every operation matching A or B has iteration=[] and also matches C. A/B specificity is (1,0,1,1,1); C specificity is (1,1,1,1,1). C is the unique maximum throughout their overlap; unrelated operations use defaults. Nevertheless check/hash exit 1, empty stdout, "§11: §11: multiple maximal matching schedule entries". All six document-order permutations reject. A/C passes; removing C correctly rejects A/B. Equal-specificity overlap is only a candidate conflict. Reject it only where its realizable intersection has no strictly more-specific matching entry of the same kind. Account for coverage by the union of higher-specificity selectors and the object’s legal invocation/iteration domains; do not merely accept a tie whenever some higher entry overlaps part of it, and do not silently pick document order.
